```python
def evaluate(rules, facts):
    if not isinstance(rules, dict):
        raise ValueError("rules must be a mapping")

    for op, keys in rules.items():
        if op == "all":
            return all(facts.get(key) for key in keys)
        if op == "any":
            return any(facts.get(key) for key in keys)
        raise ValueError("unknown rule operator: %r" % (op,))

    return True
```

Semantics: `{"all": [k...]}` → `all(...)` over listed keys; `{"any": [k...]}` → `any(...)`; missing keys are falsy (`facts.get`); empty list follows Python conventions (`all([]) == True`, `any([]) == False`); unknown operators raise `ValueError`; an empty rules mapping returns `True`.
